name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: French 10-year yield fell back below 4.9% on 20 Nov; France–Bund spread hovers near the 150bp Alert line
state: The French 10-year yield slipped back below 4.9% on 20 Nov as an equity sell-off lifted demand for government bonds, well off its October peak of 5.1% (Trading Economics). Earlier readings put the France–Bund spread at about 156bp on 16 Nov and near 149bp on 18 Nov, so it is moving either side of 150bp without a confirmed sustained close above it. France's November flash PMI showed its sharpest output fall in six months (Reuters). No failed G7 auction or emergency buying was found, so the Alert is unconfirmed and the level stays Watch.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed through to euro-area loan rates and put pressure on France's budget plans. Euro-area bond markets remain open and functioning.
rubric_hit: France–Bund ~150bp, at top of 80–150bp Watch band; no sustained close above 150bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — French OAT yields retreat as safe-haven demand rises
Reuters via Investing.com — Euro zone growth holds steady but France's deepening downturn clouds outlook, PMI shows

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
